newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: S.Lanka stocks end low on retail sale of blue chip.
newsitem.headline: S.Lanka stocks end low on retail sale of blue chip.

text.p: Sri Lanka stocks closed lower after moving in a narrow range on Tuesday, dragged down by retail selling of highly capitalised blue chips, brokers said.

The all-share index closed 2.9 points down at 821.9, with price gains and declines runing neck-and-neck at 37 to 38. Highly capitalised blue chips John Keells Holdings fell 6.75 rupees to 335.25 and Development Finance 2.25 to 308.
"John Keells and Development Finance fell sharply on very small volumes, which is probably due to a retail investor getting liquid," said Dimuthu Abeysekera of brokerage Allied Phillips Securities.
"There are institutional buyers who are willing to pay slight premiums for these same shares, provided you can give them big parcels," he added.
Turnover was a mild 40.5 million rupees, as buyers were restrained by a lack of sellers, brokers said.
"Sellers are holding on because they expect to get premiums for most stocks, once the corporate results for the period to June come out," said one broker.
Foreign buying was worth 5.4 million rupees while selling was 6.3 million rupees.
